Part IV: Class 9–10 Secondary Mathematics (माध्यमिक गणित)

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: What is the correct grammatical Sandhi-Vichhed (disjunction) of the Sanskrit loanword 'Ujjwal' (उज्ज्वल)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — Ut + Jwal (उत् + ज्वल)

• Step-by-Step Grammatical Rule:
1. This follows the Sanskrit Paninian Vyanjan Sandhi (व्यंजन संधि) assimilation rule: त्/द् + ज्/झ् ⟶ ज्ज्.
2. When dental consonant 'त्' (t) or 'द्' (d) precedes palatal consonant 'ज्' (j), the preceding dental assimilates into half 'ज्' (j).
3. Formula: उत् + ज्वल = उज्ज्वल (Ujjwal).

• Analysis of Options:
- Option A (उत् + ज्वल): Grammatically authentic Sanskrit prefix 'उत्' combining with 'ज्वल'.
- Option B (उद् + ज्वल): Hindi colloquial variation, rejected in official BPSC answer keys.
- Option C (उज् + ज्वल): Incorrect root; 'उज्' is not a recognized Sanskrit upasarg.
- Note on Orthography: In standard Devanagari spelling, 'उज्ज्वल' contains two consecutive half 'ज' (क्लीष्ट व्यंजन गुच्छ: उ + ज् + ज् + व + ल).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Consonant Sandhi (व्यंजन संधि) Rule: When 't' (त्) or 'd' (द्) is followed by 'j' (ज्) or 'jh' (झ्), the preceding 't/d' assimilates into 'j' (ज्).
aiDeepSolution.trick: In 'Ujjwal', both 'j' letters are half (consonant cluster j + j + v + l). This is a frequent BPSC question in both Sandhi and orthography (spelling test).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Students often pick 'Ud + Jwal' due to colloquial Hindi variations, but according to Paninian Sanskrit grammar and official BPSC answer keys, 'Ut' is the standard prefix.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which type of compound (Samas) is present in the compound word 'Yathashakti' (यथाशक्ति)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Avyayibhav Samas (अव्ययीभाव समास)

• Step-by-Step Grammatical Analysis:
1. Disjunction (विग्रह): यथाशक्ति = शक्ति के अनुसार (According to one's capacity).
2. First constituent (पूर्व पद): 'यथा' is an Avyaya (Indeclinable prefix) denoting proportion/extent.
3. Principal constituent: The entire compound functions as an adverbial modifier (क्रिया-विशेषण) qualifying an action (e.g., उसने यथाशक्ति दान दिया).

• Option Breakdown:
- Option A (Tatpurush): Requires elision of Karak case endings (जैसे राजपुत्र = राजा का पुत्र), which is absent here.
- Option B (Avyayibhav): Correct, as initial constituent is an indeclinable modifier.
- Option C (Karmadharaya): Requires adjective-noun or upameya-upamana relationship (जैसे नीलगगन = नीला है जो गगन).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Avyayibhav Samas: A compound where the initial constituent is an Indeclinable/Prefix (Avyaya) and is the principal element, causing the whole compound to function adverbially.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Look for prefixes like 'Yatha-', 'Prati-', 'Be-', 'Ba-', 'Bhar-', 'Anu-'. Yathashakti literally translates to 'according to one's capacity' (शक्ति के अनुसार).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Tatpurush involves elision of case endings (Karak), whereas here 'Yatha' is an indeclinable modifier.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which of the following spellings is orthographically correct in Hindi?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — Kavayitri (कवयित्री)

• Morphological Rules:
1. Gender derivation in Hindi: Masculine noun 'Kavi' (कवि) forms its feminine counterpart through the suffix '-ayitri' (अयित्री), resulting in Kav + ayitri = Kavayitri (कवयित्री).
2. Standard Syllable Sequence: क + व + यि + त्री (Note: no short 'i' matra on 'v').

• Why Options B and C are Incorrect:
- Option B (*कवियत्री): Hypercorrection placing short 'i' on 'v'.
- Option C (*कवयित्री with variation): Erroneous vowel placement.
- This is one of BPSC's most recurring spelling questions across TRE 1.0, 2.0, and 3.0.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Feminine noun formation: In Hindi/Sanskrit, the feminine counterpart of Kavi is derived as Kav + ayitri, not Kavi + yatri.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Remember the syllable pattern: Ka - va - yi - tree (no vowel mark on 'va').
aiDeepSolution.trap: Most candidates intuitively place a short 'i' on 'v' (*Kaviyatri), which is an erroneous hypercorrection.

questions.subject: Hindi Grammar
questions.question: Which prefix (Upasarg) is used in the compound word 'Atyant' (अत्यंत)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Ati (अति)

• Step-by-Step Sandhi Analysis:
1. Disjunction: अत्यंत = अति + अंत.
2. Yan Sandhi Rule: When short 'इ' (i) is followed by a dissimilar vowel like 'अ' (a), it transforms into the semi-vowel 'य्' (y).
3. Morphological breakdown: अति (Prefix) + अंत (Root noun) ⟶ अत् + य् + अंत ⟶ अत्यंत.

• Option Breakdown:
- Option A (अत्): 'अत्' is not an independent Sanskrit prefix.
- Option B (अति): Correct standard prefix meaning 'excessive' or 'beyond'.
- Option C (अत्य): Erroneous surface reading created by the phonetic assimilation.

aiDeepSolution.concept: A prefix (Upasarg) is an affix placed at the beginning of a root word. Here, 'i' of Ati combines with 'a' of Ant to form 'y' via Yan Sandhi rules.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Split the word by Sandhi: Ati + Ant = Atyant. Hence the root prefix is 'Ati'.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often superficially look at the first two letters and pick 'Atya', which is not a standard prefix.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the correct verb to fill in the blank:
'Neither the teacher nor the students _______ present in the seminar yesterday.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — were

• Syntactic Rule of Proximity:
1. Correlative Conjunctions: When subjects are conjoined by 'Neither...nor' or 'Either...or', the finite verb must agree in grammatical number and person with the closest (adjacent) subject.
2. In this sentence: 'Neither the teacher (Singular Subject 1) nor the students (Plural Subject 2) _______ present yesterday.'
3. The subject immediately preceding the blank is 'the students' (Plural).
4. Time marker: 'yesterday' specifies past simple tense.
5. Therefore, the verb must be plural past: 'were'.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Option A ('was'): Incorrect because it mistakenly agrees with the distant subject 'teacher'. If the sentence were inverted ('Neither the students nor the teacher was...'), 'was' would be correct.
- Option C ('has been'): Incorrect tense; 'yesterday' requires past simple, not present perfect.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Rule of Proximity: When two subjects are connected by correlative conjunctions 'Neither...nor' or 'Either...or', the finite verb agrees in number and person with the closest subject.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Identify the noun adjacent to the blank: 'students' (plural) -> requires plural past verb 'were' (time marker is 'yesterday').
aiDeepSolution.trap: If the sentence were inverted ('Neither the students nor the teacher...'), the verb would be singular ('was'). Here 'students' governs the verb.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the appropriate article to fill in the blank:
'He is _______ European scholar whom we met in Patna.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — a

• Phonetic Law of Indefinite Articles:
1. Indefinite article selection in English ('a' vs 'an') is strictly dictated by the initial spoken phonetic sound, not the written alphabet letter.
2. IPA Transcription: 'European' is pronounced as /ˈjʊərəˈpiːən/, opening with the voiced palatal semi-vowel glide /j/ (identical to the consonant sound in 'yellow' or 'you').
3. Because it opens with a consonant sound, it strictly requires the article 'a'.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Option A ('an'): Common trap for candidates who look at vowel letter 'E' rather than the spoken sound.
- Option C ('the'): Not applicable on first generic mention of an indefinite noun phrase.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Indefinite article choice ('a' vs 'an') is strictly determined by the initial phonetic sound of the following word, not the orthographic letter. 'European' begins with the consonant glide /juː/ (like 'you').
aiDeepSolution.trick: Words like 'a European', 'a university', 'a unicorn', 'a one-rupee note' all take 'a' because they begin with consonant phonemes /j/ or /w/.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not mechanically pick 'an' merely because the word opens with vowel letter 'E'.

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Complete the sentence with the correct conditional structure:
'If the candidate _______ harder, he would have cleared the BPSC examination.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — had worked

• Third Conditional Formula:
1. Clause Structure: If + Past Perfect (had + V3), Subject + would have + Past Participle (V3).
2. Main clause given: 'he would have cleared the BPSC examination'.
3. The sub-clause (If-clause) requires past perfect: 'had worked'.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Option A ('worked'): Simple past pairs with 'would + base verb' (Second conditional for unreal present: 'If he worked, he would clear').
- Option C ('would work'): Error; 'would' is never used in the condition clause of an If-sentence.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Third Conditional (Past Unreal Condition): If + Past Perfect (had + V3), Subject + would have + Past Participle (V3).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Notice 'would have cleared' in the main clause. It strictly pairs with 'had + V3' in the If-clause.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Using 'would have worked' in the If-clause is a common error (Conditionals never take 'would' in the If-clause).

questions.subject: English Grammar
questions.question:
Choose the correct preposition to fill in the blank:
'The live online lecture is scheduled to start _______ 8:30 AM sharp.'
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option C — at

• Rules for Prepositions of Time:
1. 'At' is used for exact points in time on a clock (at 8:30 AM, at 5 o'clock, at noon, at dawn).
2. 'On' is reserved for specific calendar days and dates (on Monday, on October 9th).
3. 'In' is used for longer durations, months, years, and centuries (in October, in 2026, in the morning).

• Distractor Breakdown:
- 'On 8:30 AM' and 'In 8:30 AM' violate standard English usage.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Prepositions of Time: Use 'at' for precise clock times and specific points of day (at 8:30 AM, at noon, at midnight).
aiDeepSolution.trick: 'At' = clock time | 'On' = days and dates | 'In' = months, years, and seasons.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not use 'in' or 'on' for specific hour markers.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: Where did the 1857 Revolt in Bihar initially break out on 12 June 1857?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option C — Rohini village (Deoghar)

• Detailed Historical Chronology in Bihar:
1. 12 June 1857: Mutiny broke out in Rohini village (Deoghar district, modern-day Jharkhand) in the headquarters of the 5th Irregular Cavalry (later 32nd Native Infantry). Major Norman Leslie was killed by mutineers.
2. 3 July 1857: Urban uprising in Patna City led by Pir Ali Khan.
3. 25 July 1857: Three native regiments (7th, 8th, 40th) mutinied at Danapur cantonment and marched to Arrah/Jagdishpur.
4. 26 July 1857: Babu Veer Kunwar Singh assumed commander-in-chief leadership of the rebel sepoys.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Option A (Jagdishpur): Kunwar Singh joined in late July 1857, more than a month after Rohini.
- Option B (Danapur): Danapur mutiny occurred on 25 July 1857.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Initial spark of 1857 in Bihar took place at Rohini village, where Lieutenant Norman Leslie was killed by mutinous soldiers.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Chronology: Rohini (12 June) ⟶ Patna (3 July) ⟶ Danapur (25 July) ⟶ Jagdishpur (26 July).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Most candidates mark Danapur or Jagdishpur, which occurred later in July 1857.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: Who led the 1857 uprising in Patna City on 3 July 1857?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Pir Ali Khan

• Detailed Historical Narrative:
1. Pir Ali Khan was a passionate nationalist and book-seller in Patna who secretly organized rebel cells against British tyranny.
2. On 3 July 1857, Pir Ali led an armed procession through Patna city holding the rebel flag.
3. During the confrontation, Dr. R. Lyell, British Opium Agent, was killed while trying to disperse the assembly.
4. Commissioner William Tayler launched a brutal crackdown; Pir Ali's house was demolished, 36 associates arrested, and Pir Ali was publicly executed by hanging on 7 July 1857.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Option A (Babu Kunwar Singh): Led the rebellion from Jagdishpur and Shahabad district.
- Option C (Amar Singh): Kunwar Singh's brother who fought guerrilla battles in the Kaimur hills in 1858.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Pir Ali Khan mobilized the local masses in Patna. In the ensuing clash, British Opium Agent Dr. R. Lyell was killed. Commissioner William Tayler suppressed the revolt and Pir Ali was publicly executed.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Patna City = Pir Ali Khan (Bookseller). Jagdishpur = Babu Kunwar Singh.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing the urban Patna revolt with the Arrah/Jagdishpur rebellion led by Kunwar Singh.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: At the age of nearly 80, which eminent leader from Jagdishpur spearheaded the 1857 rebellion and defeated British forces under Captain Dunbar and Le Grand?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Babu Veer Kunwar Singh

• Military Exploits of Kunwar Singh:
1. Leader of Shahabad: At the age of nearly 80, the zamindar of Jagdishpur organized rebel infantry and cavalry.
2. Siege of Arrah: He trapped British soldiers at the Arrah House and decisively routed Captain Dunbar's relief force (killing over 150 British soldiers).
3. Battles in UP: He campaigned across Mirzapur, Rewa, Banda, Kanpur, and Azamgarh, defeating Colonel Milman and Lord Mark Kerr.
4. Final Victory: Returning to Jagdishpur on 23 April 1858, he defeated Captain Le Grand's British forces. Having severed his own wounded left arm after being hit by a cannonball across the Ganga, he passed away on 26 April 1858.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Maulvi Ahmadullah fought primarily in Faizabad/Lucknow.
- Tatya Tope was active in Gwalior and Central India.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Kunwar Singh assumed leadership after the Danapur sepoy revolt on 25 July 1857. He defeated Dunbar near Arrah and Le Grand near Jagdishpur before succumbing to injuries on 26 April 1858.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Look for keywords 'Jagdishpur' and '80 years old' ⟶ Babu Veer Kunwar Singh.
aiDeepSolution.trap: His younger brother Amar Singh continued the guerrilla struggle after his death from the Kaimur Hills.

questions.subject: National Movement
questions.question: What proportion of land was compulsorily reserved for indigo cultivation under the Tinkathia system in Champaran?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 3/20th of land

• Agrarian Context of the Tinkathia System:
1. Unit Definition: In Bihar land revenue measurement, 1 Bigha consists of exactly 20 Kathas.
2. Colonial Exploitation: European indigo planters coerced tenant peasants (ryots) through contracts (*satta*) to cultivate indigo on 3 kathas of the best, most fertile land in every bigha (3/20 ratio).
3. Economic Ruin: Indigo cultivation exhausted soil fertility, prevented food crop cultivation, and planters paid exploitative, non-viable prices.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- 1/10th (2 kathas) and 3/10th (6 kathas) are incorrect proportions.

aiDeepSolution.concept: 1 Bigha = 20 Kathas in Bihar. 'Tin-kathia' literally means 3 kathas out of 20 kathas (3/20th).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Tinkathia = 3 kathas out of 1 Bigha (20 Kathas) = 3/20.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse 3/20 with 3/10 or 1/3.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: Who persuaded Mahatma Gandhi during the 1916 Lucknow Congress Session to visit Champaran and investigate the plight of indigo cultivators?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Rajkumar Shukla

• Historic Role of Rajkumar Shukla:
1. Background: Rajkumar Shukla was an educated and determined peasant from Murli Bharhawa village in West Champaran.
2. The Pursuit: He travelled to the 31st Session of the Indian National Congress at Lucknow in December 1916. He met Bal Gangadhar Tilak and then approached Mahatma Gandhi.
3. Persistence: When Gandhi showed reluctance due to prior commitments, Shukla followed him to Kanpur, Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad), and Calcutta until Gandhi agreed to accompany him to Champaran in April 1917.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Dr. Rajendra Prasad and Brajkishore Prasad joined Gandhi upon his arrival in Patna and Champaran, but the individual who brought him from Lucknow was Rajkumar Shukla.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Rajkumar Shukla represented the suffering peasantry of Champaran. Gandhi accompanied him to Patna, Muzaffarpur, and finally arrived in Champaran in April 1917.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Lucknow Congress 1916 invitation = Rajkumar Shukla.
aiDeepSolution.trap: While Rajendra Prasad and Brajkishore Prasad were key associates during the inquiry, the primary initiator who brought Gandhi was Rajkumar Shukla.

questions.subject: National Movement in Bihar
questions.question: As an outcome of the Champaran Satyagraha (1917), what percentage of the illegally extorted dues did European planters agree to refund?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 25%

• Compromise & Significance of the Refund:
1. Inquiry Findings: The Champaran Agrarian Enquiry Committee (headed by F.G. Sly, with Gandhi as member) unanimously found the planters guilty of illegal exactions (*sharahbeshi* and *tawan*).
2. Strategic Compromise: The planters offered a 25% refund, hoping Gandhi would demand 50% or 100% and break negotiations. Gandhi accepted 25% immediately.
3. Historical Impact: Gandhi explained that the monetary amount mattered far less than the fact that British planters had been forced to surrender their prestige and acknowledge their illegal conduct. Within a decade, the planters abandoned the estates completely.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Gandhi compromised on a 25% refund to break the prestige and moral dominance of the British planters. The Tinkathia system was formally abolished by the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Gandhi accepted 25% refund because the planters' prestige was shattered more than the monetary concession.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often assume full refund (100%) or half (50%). The exact figure is 25%.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: What is the total length of the River Ganga within the geographic territory of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 445 km

• Geographical Analysis of River Ganga in Bihar:
1. Length: The Ganga flows for exactly 445 km through the state of Bihar (out of its total national course of 2,525 km).
2. Administrative Coverage: It traverses 12 districts: Buxar, Bhojpur, Saran, Patna, Vaishali, Samastipur, Begusarai, Lakhisarai, Munger, Khagaria, Bhagalpur, and Katihar.
3. Longest Stretch: Patna district hosts the longest course of the river (~99 km), followed by Bhagalpur.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- 405 km and 525 km are incorrect figures.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Ganga has a total length of 2,525 km in India. In Bihar, its stretch is 445 km, entering at Chausa (Buxar) and exiting at Manihari (Katihar). It has its longest stretch in Patna district (~99 km).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Remember 445 km (exactly 12 districts). Patna has the longest stretch (~99 km).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse the Bihar length (445 km) with the West Bengal or UP stretches.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: Near which historic location does the River Ganga enter the state of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Chausa (Buxar)

• Course & Entry Points:
1. Entry: River Ganga crosses the UP-Bihar border near Chausa in Buxar district, forming the boundary between Buxar and Ballia (UP).
2. Exit: It exits Bihar near Manihari in Katihar district to enter Sahibganj (Jharkhand) and West Bengal.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Valmikinagar is the entry point of River Gandak from Nepal.
- Sahibganj is in Jharkhand, where the Ganga briefly touches.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Ganga enters Bihar at Chausa (Buxar) and exits near Manihari (Katihar).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Entry = Chausa (Buxar) | Exit = Manihari (Katihar).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Valmikinagar is the entry point of the Gandak river, not the Ganga.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: At which confluence point does the Kosi River ('Sorrow of Bihar') merge into the River Ganga?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Kursela (Katihar)

• Hydrological Features of Kosi River:
1. Origin: Formed by 7 Himalayan mountain streams (Saptakoshi) in Nepal/Tibet, cutting through the Himalayas.
2. Entry & Confluence: Enters Bihar at Bhimnagar (Supaul district) and flows through Saharsa and Madhepura to merge with the Ganga at Kursela in Katihar district.
3. Sorrow of Bihar: Due to immense silt load, the river frequently changes its channel; it has shifted over 120 km westward over the last 250 years.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Pahleza is where Gandak meets Ganga.
- Maner is where Son meets Ganga.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Kosi River originates as Saptakoshi in Nepal, enters Bihar at Supaul, and flows through Saharsa and Madhepura to merge with the Ganga at Kursela (Katihar).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Kosi ⟶ Kursela (K-K pairing).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Pahleza is the confluence of Gandak, while Maner is the confluence of Son.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: Which major south-bank peninsular tributary of the Ganga originates from the Amarkantak Plateau and joins the Ganga near Maner in Patna district?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Son River

• River Son Drainage Profile:
1. Origin: Originates from the Amarkantak plateau in Madhya Pradesh, east of the Narmada river source.
2. Course in Bihar: Enters Bihar at Rohtas district, forming the physical boundary between Rohtas/Bhojpur and Aurangabad/Arwal.
3. Confluence: Merges into the south bank of River Ganga near Maner (Patna district).

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Punpun meets at Fatuha.
- Falgu (Niranjana) flows past Gaya and disappears in the plains before directly joining the Ganga.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Son River enters Bihar at Rohtas district, flows between Rohtas/Bhojpur and Aurangabad/Arwal, and joins the Ganga near Maner.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Son River: Origin = Amarkantak, Entry in Bihar = Rohtas, Confluence = Maner (Patna).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Punpun meets the Ganga at Fatuha, not Maner.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: At which place does the Punpun River join the River Ganga?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — Fatuha

• Punpun River Confluence:
1. Originates in the Chota Nagpur Plateau (Palamu district, Jharkhand).
2. Enters Bihar in Aurangabad district, passes through Arwal and Patna.
3. Merges with River Ganga at Fatuha, about 25 km east of Patna city.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Munger is further east on the Ganga.
- Chhapra is where the Ghaghara merges from the north bank.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Originating in the Chota Nagpur Plateau of Jharkhand, the Punpun flows through Aurangabad, Arwal, and Patna before meeting the Ganga at Fatuha.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Punpun meets Ganga at Fatuha.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Chhapra is where the Ghaghara meets the Ganga.

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: What is the total geographical area of the state of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — 94,163 sq km

• Statistical Dimensions of Bihar:
1. Total Area: 94,163 square kilometers.
2. National Share: Represents 2.86% of the total geographical area of India.
3. National Ranking: 12th largest state in India by geographical area (after Jammu & Kashmir bifurcation).
4. Linear Extents: North to South = 345 km; East to West = 483 km.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- 84,163 sq km and 98,120 sq km are incorrect distractors.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Area = 94,163 sq km. North-to-South span = 345 km. East-to-West span = 483 km.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Mnemonic: 94-163 (94 thousand, 163).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not confuse the area with population percentages (population is 8.6% of India, 3rd largest).

questions.subject: Bihar Geography
questions.question: In the agricultural plains of South Bihar, the older alluvium (Bangar) is locally known by which name?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Karail-Kewal soil

• Soil Classification in Bihar:
1. Bangar (Old Alluvium): In South Bihar plains, this soil is locally known as 'Karail-Kewal'. It is heavy, dark-colored, clayey, with high water retention and calcareous nodules (kankar).
2. Khadar (New Alluvium): Light-colored silt deposited annually along river floodplains, highly fertile.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- Terai soil is found along the northern border with Nepal (Champaran to Kishanganj).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Karail-Kewal soil is characterized by heavy clay, high water retention, neutral to slightly alkaline pH, and presence of calcareous kankar nodules.
aiDeepSolution.trick: South Bihar Older Alluvium = Karail-Kewal. Newer Alluvium = Khadar.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Terai soil is found in the northern Himalayan border belt of West Champaran, Kishanganj.

questions.subject: Indian Polity
questions.question: On which historic date did the Constituent Assembly of India adopt, enact, and give to themselves the Constitution of India?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 26 November 1949

• Constitutional Timeline:
1. Adoption: The Constituent Assembly completed drafting and adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949 (celebrated as Samvidhan Divas / Constitution Day).
2. Selective Commencement: 16 articles (including Citizenship, Elections, Provisional Parliament) came into force immediately on 26 November 1949.
3. Full Enforcement: The remaining bulk of the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950 (commemorating the 1930 Purna Swaraj declaration).

• Distractor Breakdown:
- 26 January 1950 is the date of full commencement/enforcement, not adoption.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The Preamble explicitly states: 'In our Constituent Assembly this twenty-sixth day of November, 1949, do hereby Adopt, Enact and Give to Ourselves this Constitution.'
aiDeepSolution.trick: Adopted = 26 Nov 1949. Enforced (Republic Day) = 26 Jan 1950.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often choose 26 January 1950, which is the date of commencement/enforcement, not adoption.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7–8 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the additive inverse of the rational number -7/19?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 7/19

• Step-by-Step Mathematical Derivation:
1. Definition: The additive inverse of any number 'a' is defined as '-a' such that a + (-a) = 0 (the additive identity).
2. Given number: a = -7/19.
3. Additive Inverse: -(-7/19) = +7/19.
4. Verification: (-7/19) + (7/19) = 0/19 = 0. Confirmed!

• Distractor Breakdown:
- 19/7 is the negative reciprocal with inverted sign.
- -19/7 is the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Additive inverse of a is -a such that a + (-a) = 0 (the additive identity).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Just invert the sign: negative becomes positive, positive becomes negative.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Do not flip numerator and denominator (that is the reciprocal / multiplicative inverse).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7–8 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of -13/17?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — -17/13

• Step-by-Step Reciprocal Calculation:
1. Definition: The multiplicative inverse (reciprocal) of a non-zero rational number a/b is b/a such that (a/b) × (b/a) = 1 (the multiplicative identity).
2. Given fraction: -13/17.
3. Multiplicative Inverse: 1 / (-13/17) = -17/13.
4. Verification: (-13/17) × (-17/13) = +221/221 = 1.

• Distractor Breakdown:
- 17/13 drops the negative sign (resulting in product -1, which is incorrect).
- 13/17 is the additive inverse without reciprocation.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Multiplicative inverse of a/b is b/a such that (a/b) × (b/a) = 1. The algebraic sign remains unchanged.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Reciprocal flips the fraction upside down while keeping the negative sign.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Changing the sign to positive is an error; that confuses it with additive inverse.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 8 Mathematics
questions.question: For any non-zero rational number x, what is the product of its additive inverse and its multiplicative inverse?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option C — -1

• Universal Algebraic Identity Proof:
1. Let x be any non-zero rational number (x ≠ 0).
2. Additive Inverse of x = -x.
3. Multiplicative Inverse of x = 1/x.
4. Product = (-x) × (1/x) = - (x/x) = -1.

• Numerical Check (Let x = 4/5):
- Additive inv = -4/5
- Multiplicative inv = 5/4
- Product = (-4/5) × (5/4) = -20/20 = -1.
This holds universally for every non-zero rational number.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Universal algebraic identity: Additive Inverse × Multiplicative Inverse = (-x) × (1/x) = -1 for any x ≠ 0.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Take any sample number, e.g., 5: Additive inv = -5, Multiplicative inv = 1/5. Product = -5 × 1/5 = -1.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Thinking the product cancels out to positive +1.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6–8 Mathematics
questions.question: If the 6-digit number 473x24 is divisible by 9, what is the single-digit value of x?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 7

• Step-by-Step Divisibility Test for 9:
1. Rule: A number is divisible by 9 if and only if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.
2. Sum of digits in 473x24: 4 + 7 + 3 + x + 2 + 4 = 20 + x.
3. Find the smallest non-negative integer x (0 ≤ x ≤ 9) such that (20 + x) is a multiple of 9.
4. Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36...
5. 20 + x = 27 ⟹ x = 27 - 20 = 7.
6. Verification: 473724 ÷ 9 = 52636 (exact quotient!).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Divisibility rule for 9: A number is divisible by 9 if and only if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 9.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Sum known digits: 4 + 7 + 3 + 2 + 4 = 20. Nearest multiple of 9 > 20 is 27. x = 27 - 20 = 7.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Picking 5 gives sum 25, which is not divisible by 9.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6–8 Mathematics
questions.question: If the 7-digit number 853x412 is completely divisible by 11, what is the value of digit x?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option E — None of the above

• Step-by-Step Divisibility Test for 11:
1. Rule: Alternating sum of digits from right to left must be 0 or a multiple of 11.
2. Positions from right to left in 8 5 3 x 4 1 2:
   - Odd positions (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th): 2 + 4 + 3 + 8 = 17.
   - Even positions (2nd, 4th, 6th): 1 + x + 5 = 6 + x.
3. Difference: (Sum of odd places) - (Sum of even places) = 17 - (6 + x) = 11 - x.
4. For divisibility by 11, (11 - x) must be 0 or a multiple of 11:
   - Case 1: 11 - x = 0 ⟹ x = 11 (invalid; x must be a single digit 0–9).
   - Case 2: 11 - x = 11 ⟹ x = 0 (valid single digit!).
5. Checking options: (A) 6, (B) 4, (C) 3. Since 0 is not in options A, B, or C, the correct BPSC answer is 'None of the above' (Option E).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Divisibility rule for 11: Difference between the sum of digits in odd places and even places must be either 0 or a multiple of 11.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Calculate: Sum(Odd) - Sum(Even) = 17 - (6 + x) = 11 - x. For a single digit (0-9), only x = 0 satisfies this condition.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates often hesitate to choose 'None of the above' (Option E) even when their calculation is correct. BPSC frequently makes Option E the correct answer!

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6 Mathematics
questions.question: Three bells toll at intervals of 12, 15, and 18 seconds respectively. If they toll together now, after how many minutes will they next toll together?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 3 minutes

• Step-by-Step LCM Calculation:
1. The bells toll together at intervals equal to the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their individual periods.
2. Prime factorisation:
   - 12 = 2² × 3
   - 15 = 3 × 5
   - 18 = 2 × 3²
3. LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180 seconds.
4. Convert seconds to minutes: 180 ÷ 60 = 3 minutes.
5. Therefore, the bells will next toll together after exactly 3 minutes.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Simultaneous recurring events occur at the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of their individual time periods.
aiDeepSolution.trick: 12 = 2² × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, 18 = 2 × 3². LCM = 2² × 3² × 5 = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180 seconds. Convert to minutes: 180 / 60 = 3 minutes.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Candidates find 180 and forget to convert seconds into minutes.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the LCM of the fractions 2/3, 4/9, and 5/6?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — 20/3

• Formula for Fractions LCM:
1. Formula: LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) / (HCF of denominators).
2. Numerators: 2, 4, 5.
   - LCM(2, 4, 5) = 20.
3. Denominators: 3, 9, 6.
   - Factors: 3 = 3, 9 = 3², 6 = 2 × 3.
   - HCF(3, 9, 6) = 3.
4. Result: 20 / 3.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Standard Fraction Formula: LCM(Fractions) = LCM(Numerators) / HCF(Denominators).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Numerators = 2, 4, 5 ⟶ LCM = 20. Denominators = 3, 9, 6 ⟶ HCF = 3. Result = 20/3.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Inverting the formula (e.g., finding HCF of numerators / LCM of denominators, which gives HCF, not LCM).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6 Science
questions.question: In a laboratory test, when a few drops of dilute Iodine solution are added to a crushed food sample, it turns Blue-Black. This confirms the presence of which nutrient?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Starch

• Biochemical Mechanism:
1. Test Reagent: Dilute Iodine solution (Lugol's iodine).
2. Reaction: Starch is composed of two polysaccharides: Amylose (helical polymer) and Amylopectin (branched polymer).
3. Color Formation: Tri-iodide ions (I3⁻) fit inside the helical core of amylose coils, forming a charge-transfer complex that absorbs light and displays an intense blue-black coloration.
4. Heat sensitivity: Heating unravels the helix and the blue color disappears; cooling restores it.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Iodine intercalates into the helical amylose structure of starch, producing a characteristic deep blue-black charge-transfer complex.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Iodine ⟶ Blue-Black = Starch.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Proteins give violet with Biuret test, not blue-black with iodine.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6 Science
questions.question: Which chemical reagents are used in the Biuret test to confirm the presence of proteins in food?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — Copper Sulphate and Caustic Soda (NaOH)

• Biuret Reaction Details:
1. Reagents: A few drops of 1% Copper Sulphate (CuSO4) solution and 10 drops of 10% Caustic Soda (NaOH, Sodium Hydroxide).
2. Mechanism: In an alkaline medium provided by NaOH, copper (Cu²⁺) ions coordinate with the nitrogen atoms of four peptide bonds in the protein polypeptide chain.
3. Color: Forms a distinct violet/purple coordination complex, confirming protein presence.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Biuret reaction: Cu²⁺ ions form a violet coordination complex with peptide bonds in alkaline (NaOH) medium.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Protein Test = CuSO4 + NaOH ⟶ Violet color.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing CuSO4 with FeSO4 or iodine.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 6–7 Science
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins are completely water-soluble and must be regularly supplied in the daily diet?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Vitamins B-Complex and C

• Solubility & Storage Differences:
1. Water-Soluble: Vitamin B-complex and Vitamin C. They dissolve easily in water and are constantly excreted by the kidneys via urine. They cannot be stored in the body and must be consumed daily.
2. Fat-Soluble: Vitamins K, E, D, and A (K-E-D-A). They dissolve in lipids, are absorbed with dietary fat, and are stored in the liver and adipose tissues for months.
3. Thermal Sensitivity: Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) is extremely thermolabile and is destroyed by cooking heat.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vitamins are classified into: Fat-soluble (K, E, D, A) stored in liver/adipose tissue; and Water-soluble (B-complex, C) which cannot be stored in the body.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Mnemonic: 'K-E-D-A' is fat-soluble. 'B and C' are water-soluble.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Vitamins A, D, E, K are fat-soluble and excess can cause hypervitaminosis.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7 Science
questions.question: If two plane mirrors are placed inclined at an angle of 60° to each other, how many images of an object placed between them will be formed?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 5

• Inclined Plane Mirrors Optics:
1. Formula: If two plane mirrors are inclined at angle θ, calculate m = 360° / θ.
2. In this problem: θ = 60° ⟹ m = 360 / 60 = 6.
3. Rule: When m is an EVEN integer, the number of images formed is n = m - 1 regardless of whether the object lies symmetrically or asymmetrically.
4. Calculation: n = 6 - 1 = 5 images.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Number of images between inclined plane mirrors: When 360/θ is even, n = (360/θ) - 1 regardless of object position.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Forgetting to subtract 1 and answering 6.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7–8 Science
questions.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a concave mirror to obtain a virtual, erect, and magnified image?
options: Between the Focus (F) and Centre of Curvature (C)
More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option C — Between the Pole (P) and Focus (F)

• Ray Optics of Concave Mirror:
1. Position of Object: Placed between Pole (P) and Principal Focus (F).
2. Behavior of Rays:
   - Ray parallel to principal axis reflects through Focus.
   - Ray through Centre of Curvature reflects back along the same path.
   - The reflected rays diverge in front of the mirror, but appear to intersect behind the mirror when produced backwards.
3. Image Characteristics: Virtual, erect, and magnified (enlarged).
4. Practical Use: Dentists use concave mirrors in this specific configuration to see enlarged images of teeth.

aiDeepSolution.concept: In all other positions, a concave mirror forms a real and inverted image. Only when placed between P and F does it form a virtual, erect, and enlarged image (principle of dentist mirrors).
aiDeepSolution.trick: Dentist Mirror Case: Between P and F ⟶ Virtual, Erect, Enlarged.
aiDeepSolution.trap: At C it forms real, inverted, same size image. Between F and C it forms real, inverted, magnified image.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 7 Science
questions.source: NCERT Transportation in Animals and Plants
questions.question: Which plant vascular tissue is responsible for the bidirectional translocation of synthesized food (sucrose) from leaves to other storage organs?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Phloem

• Comparative Plant Vascular Biology:
1. Phloem:
   - Consists of sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, and phloem fibers.
   - Translocates photosynthesized organic sugars (sucrose) from sources (leaves) to sinks (roots, buds, fruits).
   - Transport direction is bidirectional (both upward and downward).
   - Active process requiring ATP energy.
2. Xylem:
   - Transports water and inorganic mineral ions from roots to leaves.
   - Conduction is strictly unidirectional (upward only), driven passively by transpiration pull.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Phloem transports food (sucrose) in both upward and downward directions (bidirectional translocation) using energy (ATP). Xylem conducts water and minerals unidirectionally upwards.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Phloem = Food (bidirectional) | Xylem = Water/Jal (unidirectional).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing Xylem (water) with Phloem (food).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 8 Science
questions.question: If the amplitude of a sound wave is tripled, by what factor will the loudness of the sound increase?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option C — 9 times

• Physical Law of Acoustic Intensity:
1. Relationship: The loudness (and acoustic energy/intensity) of a sound wave is directly proportional to the square of the amplitude of vibration: Loudness ∝ (Amplitude)².
2. When Amplitude A is tripled (A' = 3A):
   - Loudness' ∝ (3A)² = 9A² = 9 × Original Loudness.
3. Frequency vs Amplitude:
   - Amplitude controls Loudness (measured in decibels).
   - Frequency controls Pitch / Shrillness (measured in Hertz).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Physics of Sound: Loudness ∝ A². Pitch is determined by frequency, whereas loudness/intensity is determined by amplitude squared.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Loudness ∝ A² ⟶ (3)² = 9 times.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Assuming linear relationship (3 times).

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: According to the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, every composite number can be factorized as a product of prime numbers in a manner that is:
options: Unique, apart from the order in which prime factors occur
More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Unique, apart from the order in which prime factors occur

• Mathematical Statement & NCERT Theorem 1.2:
1. Statement: Every composite natural number can be expressed (factorized) as a product of prime numbers, and this factorisation is completely unique, apart from the order in which prime factors are written.
2. Canonical Prime Factorisation: Any integer n can be uniquely written as n = p₁ᵃ¹ · p₂ᵃ² · ... · pₖᵃᵏ where p₁ < p₂ < ... < pₖ are primes.
3. Example: 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. While the order can be written as 3 × 5 × 2 or 5 × 2 × 3, the prime factors (2, 3, 5) and their powers are unique.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Theorem 1.2 (NCERT Class 10): Every composite number can be factored uniquely as a product of primes, apart from the order in which the prime factors occur.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Fundamental Theorem = Unique Prime Factorization.
aiDeepSolution.trap: The order can change (e.g., 2 × 3 = 3 × 2), but the set of prime factors and their multiplicities are strictly unique.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: A rational number p/q in simplest form (gcd(p, q) = 1) has a terminating decimal expansion if and only if the prime factorisation of q contains:
options: Only primes of the form 2^n · 5^m (n, m non-negative integers)
More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Only primes of the form 2^n · 5^m (n, m non-negative integers)

• Rigorous Mathematical Proof:
1. Let rational number in reduced form be x = p/q (with gcd(p, q) = 1).
2. If x has a terminating decimal expansion of k digits, it can be written as x = N / 10ᵏ.
3. Since 10 = 2 × 5, 10ᵏ = 2ᵏ · 5ᵏ.
4. Thus the denominator q in reduced form must be a divisor of 10ᵏ, meaning prime factors of q can ONLY be 2 and/or 5.
5. If any other prime (like 3, 7, 11) divides q, the fraction yields a non-terminating recurring decimal.

aiDeepSolution.concept: NCERT Theorem: Let x = p/q be a rational number such that prime factorisation of q is of the form 2^n · 5^m. Then x has a terminating decimal expansion.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Terminating decimal denominator must ONLY have factors of 2 and/or 5.
aiDeepSolution.trap: If any other prime (like 3, 7, 11) is present in the reduced denominator, the decimal is non-terminating repeating.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: After how many decimal places will the decimal expansion of 13 / 1250 terminate?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option C — 4 decimal places

• Step-by-Step Calculation:
1. Fraction: 13 / 1250. Check if reduced: gcd(13, 1250) = 1 (yes).
2. Prime factorize denominator 1250:
   - 1250 = 2 × 625 = 2¹ × 5⁴.
3. Powers: n = 1 (power of 2), m = 4 (power of 5).
4. Theorem: Decimal terminates after max(n, m) places = max(1, 4) = 4 places.
5. Calculation check: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2³ = 8:
   - (13 × 8) / (2¹ × 2³ × 5⁴) = 104 / (2⁴ × 5⁴) = 104 / 10,000 = 0.0104 (exactly 4 decimal places!).

aiDeepSolution.concept: The decimal expansion of p / (2^n · 5^m) terminates after exactly max(n, m) places.
aiDeepSolution.trick: 1250 = 2 × 625 = 2^1 × 5^4. The highest power between 1 and 4 is 4. Hence, terminates after 4 places (0.0104).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Counting only the power of 2 or taking the sum 1+4=5.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the geometric shape of the graph of the quadratic polynomial P(x) = ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option C — Parabola

• Coordinate Geometry of Polynomial Graphs:
1. Linear Polynomial (P(x) = ax + b): Graph is a Straight Line.
2. Quadratic Polynomial (P(x) = ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0): Graph is a Parabola.
3. Orientation:
   - If leading coefficient a > 0: The parabola opens upwards (∪).
   - If leading coefficient a < 0: The parabola opens downwards (∩).
4. Zeros: The x-coordinates of the points where the parabola intersects the x-axis are the real zeros of the polynomial.

aiDeepSolution.concept: The graph of y = ax² + bx + c is a parabola. It intersects the x-axis at at most 2 points, corresponding to its real zeros.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Linear = Straight line | Quadratic = Parabola.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Parabolas are not hyperbolas or circles.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If α and β are the zeros of the quadratic polynomial P(x) = 3x² - 5x - 2, what is the sum of its zeros (α + β)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 5/3

• Step-by-Step Calculation:
1. Standard quadratic form: ax² + bx + c = 0.
2. Given: 3x² - 5x - 2. Identify coefficients:
   - a = 3
   - b = -5
   - c = -2
3. Vieta's Formula for Sum of Zeros:
   - α + β = -b / a = -(-5) / 3 = 5/3.
4. Verification: Factorizing 3x² - 6x + x - 2 = 3x(x - 2) + 1(x - 2) = (3x + 1)(x - 2) = 0.
   - Roots: α = 2, β = -1/3.
   - Sum = 2 + (-1/3) = 6/3 - 1/3 = 5/3. Verified!

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vieta's formula for quadratic ax² + bx + c: Sum of roots α + β = -b/a.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Forgetting the negative sign in -b/a and answering -5/3.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If α and β are the zeros of the quadratic polynomial P(x) = 2x² + 7x + 5, what is the product of its zeros (αβ)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 5/2

• Step-by-Step Calculation:
1. Given polynomial: 2x² + 7x + 5.
2. Coefficients: a = 2, b = 7, c = 5.
3. Vieta's Formula for Product of Zeros:
   - αβ = c / a = 5 / 2.
4. Verification:
   - Factorizing 2x² + 5x + 2x + 5 = x(2x + 5) + 1(2x + 5) = (2x + 5)(x + 1) = 0.
   - Roots: α = -5/2, β = -1.
   - Product = (-5/2) × (-1) = 5/2. Verified!

aiDeepSolution.concept: For ax² + bx + c, product of zeros is αβ = c/a.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Putting a negative sign on c/a.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If α and β are the zeros of the polynomial P(x) = ax² + bx + c (a, c ≠ 0), what is the value of (1/α + 1/β)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — -b/c

• Algebraic Derivation:
1. Take LCM of the denominators:
   - 1/α + 1/β = (β + α) / (αβ) = (α + β) / (αβ).
2. Substitute Vieta's formulas:
   - Sum α + β = -b/a
   - Product αβ = c/a
3. Divide the expressions:
   - (1/α + 1/β) = (-b/a) ÷ (c/a) = (-b/a) × (a/c) = -b/c.
4. Direct Exam Application: Never calculate roots individually; directly write -b/c!

aiDeepSolution.concept: Sum of reciprocals: 1/α + 1/β = (α + β)/(αβ). Since α + β = -b/a and αβ = c/a, the ratio is (-b/a)/(c/a) = -b/c.
aiDeepSolution.trick: 1/α + 1/β is always equal to -b/c. Direct exam shortcut!
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing with -b/a or +b/c.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If in the quadratic polynomial ax² + bx + c, all three coefficients a, b, and c are positive (a > 0, b > 0, c > 0), then both its zeros are:
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — Both negative

• Mathematical Sign Deduction:
1. Given: a > 0, b > 0, c > 0 in ax² + bx + c = 0.
2. Product of roots: αβ = c/a. Since both c and a are positive, c/a > 0.
   - A positive product means that both roots must have the SAME algebraic sign (either both positive or both negative).
3. Sum of roots: α + β = -b/a. Since b > 0 and a > 0, -b/a is strictly negative (< 0).
4. Conclusion: Two numbers with the same sign whose sum is negative must BOTH be strictly negative.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Sign analysis of quadratic roots: αβ = c/a > 0 means roots have identical signs. α + β = -b/a < 0 means their sum is negative. Therefore, both roots must be negative.
aiDeepSolution.trick: All positive coefficients ⟶ both roots are negative.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Assuming positive coefficients yield positive roots.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: If one of the zeros of the cubic polynomial P(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d is 0, what is the product of the other two zeros?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — c/a

• Cubic Vieta's Relations Proof:
1. Standard cubic polynomial: P(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d.
2. The pairwise product relation is: αβ + βγ + γα = c/a.
3. Let one zero be zero: γ = 0.
4. Substitute γ = 0 into the equation:
   - αβ + β(0) + (0)α = c/a
   - αβ + 0 + 0 = c/a ⟹ αβ = c/a.
5. Therefore, the product of the remaining two non-zero roots is simply c/a.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Vieta's relations for cubic: α + β + γ = -b/a, αβ + βγ + γα = c/a, αβγ = -d/a. If γ = 0, then the sum of pairwise products simplifies directly to αβ = c/a.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Put γ = 0 into αβ + βγ + γα = c/a ⟶ αβ = c/a.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing with -d/a.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 9 Mathematics
questions.question: What is the remainder when the polynomial P(x) = 2x³ - 3x² + 4x - 5 is divided by (x - 2)?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option A — 7

• Step-by-Step Remainder Theorem:
1. Theorem: When polynomial P(x) is divided by linear binomial (x - a), the remainder is equal to P(a).
2. Divisor: (x - 2) ⟹ a = 2.
3. Evaluate P(2) in P(x) = 2x³ - 3x² + 4x - 5:
   - P(2) = 2(2)³ - 3(2)² + 4(2) - 5
   - = 2(8) - 3(4) + 8 - 5
   - = 16 - 12 + 8 - 5
   - = 4 + 8 - 5 = 12 - 5 = 7.
4. Therefore, the remainder is 7.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Remainder Theorem: When P(x) is divided by (x - a), the remainder is P(a).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Performing long polynomial division when direct substitution takes 10 seconds.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 9 Mathematics
questions.question: According to the Factor Theorem, a linear polynomial (x - a) is a factor of polynomial P(x) if and only if:
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — P(a) = 0

• Factor Theorem Explanation:
1. By polynomial division algorithm: P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + R, where R = P(a).
2. Definition of Factor: A polynomial (x - a) is defined as an exact factor of P(x) if and only if the remainder of the division is zero (R = 0).
3. Since Remainder = P(a), the condition is P(a) = 0.
4. Converse: If P(a) = 0, then (x - a) is a factor of P(x).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Factor Theorem is a corollary of the Remainder Theorem: P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + P(a). If remainder P(a) = 0, then (x - a) is a factor.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Factor condition = Remainder P(a) is zero.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing P(a) = 0 with P(0) = a.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.source: NCERT Chapter 3 Pair of Linear Equations
questions.question: Under which condition does a pair of linear equations a1·x + b1·y + c1 = 0 and a2·x + b2·y + c2 = 0 represent two intersecting straight lines with a UNIQUE solution?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2

• Comprehensive Linear System Conditions:
1. Unique Solution (Consistent & Independent):
   - Condition: a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2
   - Geometry: The two straight lines have different slopes and intersect at exactly one unique point (x, y).
2. Infinitely Many Solutions (Consistent & Dependent):
   - Condition: a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2
   - Geometry: Coincident lines (one line lies completely on top of the other).
3. No Solution (Inconsistent):
   - Condition: a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2
   - Geometry: Parallel lines (same slope, different y-intercepts, never meet).

aiDeepSolution.concept: Linear system geometric conditions: 1. Unique solution (intersecting) ⟶ a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2. 2. Infinitely many (coincident) ⟶ a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2. 3. No solution (parallel) ⟶ a1/a2 = b1/b2 ≠ c1/c2.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Unique solution = Slopes are unequal = a1/a2 ≠ b1/b2.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Confusing with the condition for coincident or parallel lines.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: For what value of k will the system of equations 2x + 3y = 7 and (k - 1)x + (k + 2)y = 3k have INFINITELY MANY solutions?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 7

• Step-by-Step Parameter Solution:
1. Given equations:
   - 2x + 3y = 7 ⟹ a1 = 2, b1 = 3, c1 = 7
   - (k - 1)x + (k + 2)y = 3k ⟹ a2 = (k - 1), b2 = (k + 2), c2 = 3k
2. Condition for infinitely many solutions:
   - a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2
   - 2 / (k - 1) = 3 / (k + 2) = 7 / (3k)
3. Cross-multiply first two ratios:
   - 2(k + 2) = 3(k - 1)
   - 2k + 4 = 3k - 3
   - 4 + 3 = 3k - 2k ⟹ k = 7.
4. Check consistency with third ratio:
   - 2 / (7 - 1) = 2/6 = 1/3.
   - 3 / (7 + 2) = 3/9 = 1/3.
   - 7 / (3 × 7) = 7/21 = 1/3.
   - All ratios equal 1/3! Confirmed k = 7.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Infinitely many solutions condition: a1/a2 = b1/b2 = c1/c2.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Cross multiply 2(k+2) = 3(k-1) ⟶ 2k + 4 = 3k - 3 ⟶ k = 7. Verify: 2/6 = 3/9 = 7/21 = 1/3 (holds true!).
aiDeepSolution.trap: Not verifying with the constant ratio c1/c2.

questions.subject: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics
questions.question: A motor boat can travel at 15 km/h in still water. If the river stream flows at 3 km/h, what is the time taken by the boat to travel 36 km downstream?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation:
• Correct Answer: Option B — 2 hours

• Step-by-Step Kinematics Solution:
1. Given data:
   - Speed of boat in still water (u) = 15 km/h
   - Speed of stream current (v) = 3 km/h
   - Distance to travel = 36 km
2. Direction: Downstream (boat travels with the stream current).
3. Effective Downstream Speed = u + v = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h.
4. Time Taken = Distance ÷ Speed = 36 km ÷ 18 km/h = 2 hours.

• Comparison with Upstream:
- If it had been upstream, speed = u - v = 15 - 3 = 12 km/h, taking 36 / 12 = 3 hours.

aiDeepSolution.concept: Boat & Stream Kinematics: Downstream speed = u + v, Upstream speed = u - v.
aiDeepSolution.trick: Downstream = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h. Time = 36 / 18 = 2 hours.
aiDeepSolution.trap: Using upstream speed (15 - 3 = 12 km/h ⟶ 36/12 = 3 hours) instead of downstream.
